title: Scalar restriction of augmented Roos cones with resolution-normalized units
statement:
Let $Z$ be a scheme, $i:C\to R$ a morphism of commutative ring sheaves on a small skeleton of $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$, and $r:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(C)$ scalar restriction [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For a strict inverse tower $W$ of possibly unbounded cochain complexes, let $B_W=\prod_{n\geq1}W_n$ degreewise, $F_W=1-s_W$ with $(s_Ww)_n=t_nw_{n+1}$, and
$$\mathsf R(W)=\operatorname{Cone}(F_W)[-1],\quad \mathsf R(W)^q=B_W^{q-1}\oplus B_W^q,\quad D(y,x)=(-dy-F_Wx,dx)$$
[def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. Restriction $r$ is exact; its canonical product comparison $rB_W\cong B_{rW}$ is the identity on tuples of sections and respects projections, differentials, and $F_W$. Finite direct sums are unchanged. Thus the coordinate formula gives a natural chain isomorphism $c_W:r\mathsf R(W)\cong\mathsf R(rW)$.

For a strict tower isomorphism $f:W\cong W'$ over either ring, the diagonal product formula defines a chain isomorphism $\mathsf R(f)(y,x)=((\prod f_n)y,(\prod f_n)x)$, with inverse the diagonal product of $f_n^{-1}$. The same diagonal formula defines the chain map for any strict tower map. A transition-compatible homotopy $h$ induces the Roos homotopy $(y,x)\mapsto(-h^\Pi y,h^\Pi x)$, where $h^\Pi=\prod_nh_n$. For any compatible chain augmentation $b:L\to W$, write $b^\Pi=(b_n)_n$ and $\alpha_W(b)(z)=(0,b^\Pi z)$. This is a chain map. If $f_nr(b_n)=b'_nv$ for a strict tower map $f:rW\to W'$ and a chain map $v:rL\to L'$, then
$$\mathsf R(f)c_W\,r\alpha_W(b)=\alpha_{W'}(b')v.$$
The same formula without $r,c_W$ holds for maps over one ring.

Write $Q_R,Q_C$ for derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. There are natural isomorphisms in the respective derived categories
$$\rho_W:Q_R\mathsf R(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\!\lim W,$$
where $R\!\lim$ is total right derived ordinary inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]; these are the comparisons of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] over $R$ and over $C$. For every K-injective tower resolution $q:W\to I$, both arrows in $\mathsf R(W)\xrightarrow{\mathsf R(q)}\mathsf R(I)\xleftarrow{j_I}\lim I_n$ are quasi-isomorphisms, where $j_I(z)=(0,(z_n)_n)$, and $\rho_W$ is this zigzag followed by the universal derived-limit unit on $I$. Under $\rho_W$, $Q_R\alpha_W(b)$ is the actual canonical augmented map $Q_RL\to R\!\lim W$: the constant-tower unit followed by $R\!\lim(b)$. This equality holds also when that unit is computed using a separate resolution $\Delta L\to I'$ and a comparison $I'\to I$ commuting with the augmented map up to homotopy. The resulting isomorphism $D(r)(R\!\lim W)\cong R\!\lim(rW)$ obtained from $Q_Cc_W$ and the two $\rho$'s respects these canonical augmented maps and is natural in strict maps. No boundedness or completeness assumption is made.

proof.text: Scalar restriction composed with the faithful forgetful functor to abelian sheaves is definitionally the original forgetful functor. The module-sheaf colimit/limit theorem and reflection therefore give preservation of limits and colimits. Apply exact products on the pro-etale site over each ring.

Use the already-proved roos_cone_d and roos_cone_coords from StrictRoosDerivation for the shifted mapping-cone differential in its canonical coordinates. The existing strict-map formula gives maps and inverses. Apply the strict Roos homotopy theorem and product projection extensionality to identify its product homotopy with productHomotopy. Prove augmentation naturality by the two biproduct coordinates and product projections.

The additive Roos comparison gives the scalar cone isomorphism with the canonical product comparison. Coordinate extensionality identifies its naturality witnesses with roosF.map. Product projections show compatibility with one minus shift. The two coordinates and the given compatibility equation prove the scalar augmentation identity.

Use the explicit Roos derived universal pair and uniqueness of right derived functors to obtain rho with Q(roosι) rho = eta. The arbitrary-K-injective strict Roos comparison identifies roosι as a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of rho gives preservation of quasi-isomorphisms and the normalization formula with epsilon=Q(roosι) and d=eta_I RF(Qq) inverse. The augmentation equation follows from roosAugment_eq and the unit equation.

For a separate constant-tower resolution, compose the constant augmentation with Roos(p) and identify it with lam roosι_J by product projections. Apply the strict Roos homotopy theorem to the supplied comparison homotopy; its localization equates the two augmented composites. Naturality of roosι, the unit equation, and cancellation of RF(Qq) give precisely the separate-resolution clause.

Set Dr to the exact functor induced on derived categories and phi to its localization factorization. Define beta as Dr(rhoR inverse), phi, Q(c), rhoC. Naturality follows successively from rhoR inverse, phi, c, rhoC. The chain augmentation identity and the same naturality equations prove the final derived augmentation identity.
